verifications.claim: Boeing builds the core stage of the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'SLS built by Boeing'; R2: 'Space Launch System, built by Boeing'; R4: 'NASA has finalized its contract with Boeing... for... core stages'; R7: 'Boeing is responsible for building the core stage'; R9: 'core stage for Artemis I, built at Michoud Assembly Facility in Louisiana by Boeing'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Boeing builds the SLS core stage.

verifications.claim: Northrop Grumman provides the solid rocket boosters for the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'SLS rocket... built by Boeing and Northrop Grumman'; R5: 'Northrop Grumman' as prime for SLS; R7: 'Northrop Grumman is building the solid boosters'; R10: 'Northrop Grumman manufactures the five-segment solid rocket boosters for the NASA Space Launch System (SLS)'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm Northrop Grumman provides SLS boosters.

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne is an L3Harris company.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Aerojet Rocketdyne, an L3Harris Technologies Company'

verifications.claim: Aerojet Rocketdyne produces the RS-25 engines for the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'NASA’s prime contractors for SLS include Aerojet Rocketdyne'; R7: 'Aerojet Rocketdyne is building the engines [RS-25]'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Aerojet Rocketdyne's role in SLS engines, specifically RS-25 from context.

verifications.claim: Lockheed Martin builds the Orion spacecraft.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion spacecraft built by Lockheed Martin'; R2: 'Orion crew capsule – built by Lockheed Martin'; R5: 'Lockheed Martin is the lead contractor... for Orion'; R8: 'Lockheed Martin is the prime contractor building Orion'

verifications.claim: Boeing produces the 212-foot core stage for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '212-foot core stage'; R4: '212-foot-tall core stage... Boeing will produce SLS core stages'
verifications.reasoning: Exact dimensions and Boeing's role directly matched.

verifications.claim: The 212-foot core stage houses the main engines and flight systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '212-foot core stage propelled by four engines'; R4: 'Each SLS rocket configuration uses the same 212-foot-tall core stage to produce more than 2 million pounds of thrust'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports housing main engines; flight systems implied as core stage backbone.

verifications.claim: Northrop Grumman manufactures the twin five-segment solid rocket boosters for the Artemis missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'two... solid rocket boosters'; R9: 'two five-segment solid rocket boosters (SRBs)'; R10: 'five-segment solid rocket boosters... Northrop Grumman manufactures'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on manufacturer, twin, and five-segment description.

verifications.claim: The twin five-segment solid rocket boosters provide 75% of the thrust at launch.
verifications.label: OMITTED

verifications.claim: Airbus builds the European Service Module (ESM) for the Orion capsule for the European Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of Airbus building ESM for ESA/Orion.

verifications.claim: United Launch Alliance (ULA) developed the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute ICPS development to ULA.

verifications.claim: The SLS is managed by NASA.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS)'; R4: 'NASA’s Space Launch System rocket'; R5: 'NASA’s SLS'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe SLS as NASA's rocket/program.

verifications.claim: SLS components are manufactured across the U.S. and in Europe.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'more than 2,700 suppliers across 47 states... SLS components'; ESA/Airbus for Orion ESM (related but not SLS)
verifications.reasoning: US manufacturing clear; Europe mentioned for Orion ESM, not explicitly SLS components.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew's journey in space has begun.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R2: 'mission is scheduled to launch on April 1' (future); R8: 'completion of the historic Artemis II mission' (past)
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: some pre-launch (future), one post-mission (completed, implying begun).
